title: Many Nitnem meanings describe the verse from a distance instead of giving its meaning, and call Guru Sahib "the poet" or "the speaker"
composition_or_verse: Chaupai, Savaiye, Rehras, Anand (especially pauri 40), Sohila
evidence: Automated screen: 157 of 3,773 entries (Chaupai 46/116, Rehras Chaupai 32/100, Rehras shabad rows 11/23, Savaiye 10/40, Anand 23/208, Sohila 6/56, Jaap 10/782, Japji 4/385, Sukhmani 4/2,027) — reviews/claude-independent/evidence/m07b_reporting_voice_broadened.json. Reading by hand found more: 32 of 56 Chaupai lines read, 5 of 6 lines of Anand pauri 40 — reviews/claude-independent/evidence/m05_manual_reading.json. Examples: "ਹਮਰੀ ਕਰੋ ਹਾਥ ਦੈ ਰੱਛਾ" → "An opening request for Divine protection."; "ਦੂਖ ਰੋਗ ਸੰਤਾਪ ਉਤਰੇ ਸੁਣੀ ਸਚੀ ਬਾਣੀ" → "…are described as lifted by hearing the true Bani." title: Chaupai and Savaiye: meanings soften or change what the line says
location: nitnem/learning/course.complete.json → closeTextNotes for savaiye and chaupai
evidence: reviews/claude-independent/evidence/m05_manual_reading.json. The best-known line of the Savaiye, "ਸਾਚੁ ਕਹੋਂ ਸੁਨ ਲੇਹੁ ਸਭੈ ਜਿਨ ਪ੍ਰੇਮ ਕੀਓ ਤਿਨ ਹੀ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਪਾਇਓ", is given as "The stanza culminates in a striking affirmation that love is the way to encounter the Divine." "ਕੂਰ ਕ੍ਰਿਆ ਉਰਝਿਓ ਸਭ ਹੀ ਜਗ" becomes "can leave people…". Chaupai 24.3 adds "seeks its sustaining protection", which is not in the line. Enemies (ਦੁਸਟ, ਸੱਤ੍ਰੁ, ਬੈਰਿਨ) are regularly turned into abstract "forces".
why_it_matters: Readers are given a milder text than the one Guru Sahib wrote. Whether and how to explain strong lines is a decision for the owner and qualified teachers, not something to do silently inside the meaning.
proposed_correction: Give the plain meaning; put historical or pastoral context in the labelled note; let qualified reviewers decide wording for martial vocabulary.
acceptance_test: Each listed line reviewed and signed; meaning and note are separate fields on screen.

title: Modern legal- and medical-style disclaimers are attached to hundreds of lines
location: nitnem/learning/course.complete.json → interpretiveCaution (shown under "Interpretation and context", nitnem/learning/learning-ui.js:84); studies in all three data sets
composition_or_verse: 309 of 1,361 Nitnem line notes (148 distinct texts) and 154 of 610 studies
evidence: Examples shown to readers: "…not clinical efficacy data, and should not be used to dissuade anyone from medical treatment."; "…not a psychiatric treatment guarantee."; "…not a medical anatomy guide, yoga instruction or objective experimental map." Jaap chhand 1 brings in a present-day caste-injustice frame. Counted by script in this review. Root cause found in comparison: the builder's own test (tests/nitnem-content.mjs:219) fails unless every one of the 1,361 line notes has a caution, so a caution was written even where there was nothing to caution about.
why_it_matters: A reader opening the meaning of a line of Gurbani meets risk-management language written for a different purpose. Modern ideas are mixed into the explanation without being labelled as the editor's reflection.
proposed_correction: Make the caution field optional and drop the test rule that requires one on every line. Remove these from line notes. Put one short, respectful general note in About. Keep genuine interpretive notes (alternative readings, grammar) only.
acceptance_test: Disclaimer screen returns 0 on line notes; one general note exists; reviewers approve remaining notes.

title: Editor's working notes and talk about "the app" and "this draft" appear in what readers see
location: nitnem/learning/course.complete.json (jaap001 vocabulary "…; verify grammar"; anand25 "Exact morphology of the jeweled phrase needs review."; Jaap 7.1, 9.3, 11.4 "…gloss remains provisional"); js/japji-lessons.js (34 of 42 studies mention "this draft" or "the app")
composition_or_verse: Jaap 1, 7, 9, 11; Anand 25; Japji studies
evidence: Counted by script; e.g. a Japji teach-back question asks why "the app" counts 42 display units. In jaap001 the word ਅਨਭਉ is glossed "Self-existent", which is not its sense.
why_it_matters: Readers should meet the teaching, not the production process.
proposed_correction: Move such notes to a reviewer-only field; correct the ਅਨਭਉ gloss.
acceptance_test: Screen for "verify", "needs review", "provisional", "this draft", "the app" in reader-facing fields returns 0.

title: The screen says "Meaning" where the data itself says "selective paraphrase, not literal translation"
location: nitnem/learning/learning-ui.js:77 ("Draft meaning · tap to explore"); nitnem/index.html (depth button "Meaning"); data kind SELECTIVE_EDUCATIONAL_PARAPHRASE_NOT_LITERAL_TRANSLATION, status DRAFT_AI_UNREVIEWED
composition_or_verse: All six Nitnem readers
evidence: Verified in code and on screen. "Draft" is shown; "paraphrase, not translation" and "written with AI assistance, not yet reviewed by a qualified person" are not shown at the line.
why_it_matters: Honest labelling is one of the app's own promises.
proposed_correction: Say plainly, once per bani and in About: "Simple draft explanation written with AI assistance. Not a translation. Not yet reviewed by a qualified person."
acceptance_test: Statement visible within one tap from any meaning; identical wording in all three readers.

title: Study material is mostly in English; Punjabi study text is missing for most Nitnem passages
composition_or_verse: Punjabi study fields exist for 79 of 199 Jaap passages, 1 of 40 Anand, 0 of 10 Savaiye, 0 of 29 Chaupai, 0 of 5 Sohila, 0 of 44 Rehras
evidence: Average characters English/Punjabi per study: Japji 2,703/582; Sukhmani pauri 1,043/550; Jaap 1,373/452; Chaupai 721/83; Rehras 895/85. Counted by script from the shipped files.
why_it_matters: A Punjabi-reading elder or a learner who wants to study in Punjabi gets far less than an English reader.
proposed_correction: Write Punjabi study text first-class, not as a shortened translation.
acceptance_test: Every study has Punjabi focus, close reading, reflection and teach-back; length ratio within 0.7–1.3.

title: Punjabi spelling is not uniform; Sukhmani transliteration is mechanical
composition_or_verse: ਵਿਚ 58 / ਵਿੱਚ 2,051; ਇਕ 21 / ਇੱਕ 519; ਇਥੇ 55 / ਇੱਥੇ 151; e.g. "gauRee sukhamanee mah 5 ||"
evidence: reviews/claude-independent/evidence/m_screens.json.
why_it_matters: Polish; matters for a product that aims at excellent Punjabi.
proposed_correction: Adopt one spelling list; one transliteration scheme, labelled approximate.
acceptance_test: Spelling screen returns one form per word.

title: Checks that passed: every line has its own English and Punjabi entry; no sign of copying from published translations; cited page numbers are right
composition_or_verse: 3,773 lines ↔ 3,773 pairs; 3,388 carry the hash of their line, none stale; 259 studies cite page numbers, all correct
evidence: reviews/claude-independent/evidence/m_screens.json, reviews/claude-independent/evidence/m_compare_summary.json (of 3,748 comparable lines, 4 share a run of eight or more words with a published translation).
why_it_matters: Good foundations to build on.

title: Against the six-level learning standard, three levels are thin or absent
composition_or_verse: Read: present. Understand: present as drafts (not for 27 Rehras blocks). Word-by-word: absent — only 2 to 8 selected words per passage, marked "working gloss, not approved". Deep study: fuller for Japji and Sukhmani, thin for the Nitnem set. Cross-scriptural: 1 reference in 610 studies. Reflection: present (prompt plus private note)
evidence: Counted by script from the shipped study files (reviews/claude-independent/evidence/m_screens.json and the study field census in this review).
why_it_matters: The stated aim is a learner who understands each word, the grammar, and how the same idea appears elsewhere in Gurbani.
proposed_correction: See the learning blueprint (deliverable 8): word records with sourced origins, then cross-references reviewed by scholars.
acceptance_test: For a pilot bani every word opens a sourced entry and every passage has at least one reviewed cross-reference.

title: Nothing brings a learner back to what they saved
composition_or_verse: Saved lines and notes are lists only; no saved words; no "revisit" view
evidence: Observed in all three readers.
why_it_matters: Understanding fades without return; this can be done quietly, without streaks or scores.
proposed_correction: A calm "Return to" list ordered by time since last visit; opt-in; on-device only.
acceptance_test: A saved line reappears in the list after a set interval; nothing is counted or scored.

title: No streaks, scores, badges or nudges were found
evidence: Code and screens searched.
why_it_matters: Matches the stated values.

title: Three readers that look and behave differently
location: full-japji.html + js/japji-full.js; nitnem/index.html + nitnem/reader.js; sukhmani.html + js/sukhmani-reader.js
composition_or_verse: Japji, the six Nitnem banis, Sukhmani
evidence: Different colours (gold/green), different names for the same control, different guide behaviour, different maximum text size (48/60), different ways to save a line, different resume behaviour, separate storage and separate backups. Screenshots reviews/claude-independent/evidence/screenshots/03_jaap_read_top.png, 14_sukhmani_meaning.png; reviews/claude-independent/evidence/ua_remaining.json, u09_u15.json.
why_it_matters: A family learns the app three times. Every fix must be made three times.
proposed_correction: One reader, one data shape, one saved-learning store (see implementation plan).
acceptance_test: The same test script passes unchanged against all nine compositions.

title: Nitnem reader: a screen of headings and counts before the first line; switching to Study shows no change where you are reading
composition_or_verse: All six Nitnem readers
evidence: Screenshots reviews/claude-independent/evidence/screenshots/03_jaap_read_top.png, 06_jaap_study.png. The study block sits after the passage's last line, off screen.
why_it_matters: The reader came to read; and a button that seems to do nothing teaches people not to press it.
proposed_correction: Gurbani within the first screen; on Study, bring the study block into view or show a clear pointer.
acceptance_test: First verse line visible without scrolling at 390×664; pressing Study changes what is on screen.

title: Engineering words on family-facing screens
composition_or_verse: "tokens per minute", "30px", "70 pace", "selected expanded29-group reading", "ends after25", "All40 pauris", "Jaap Sahib · Jaap Sahib · Chhand 1", "SGGS Rehras Hymn 1", "385 frozen Gurmukhi occurrences", "Digital collation found 384 matches after HTML spacing normalization"
evidence: reviews/claude-independent/evidence/u09_u15.json and screenshots.
why_it_matters: An elder or child cannot use what they cannot read.
proposed_correction: Plain words in English and Punjabi ("Slower / Faster", "Text size"); move technical detail to an About page.
acceptance_test: A plain-language review of every visible string by a Punjabi-speaking family tester.

title: Dark mode has to be switched on in four places
composition_or_verse: Home, Nitnem, Japji, Sukhmani
evidence: Each keeps its own setting; only the Nitnem reader follows the phone's dark setting. Tested in this review.
why_it_matters: A reader at amrit vela opens the next bani and is hit by a bright page.
proposed_correction: One appearance setting for the whole app, following the phone by default.
acceptance_test: Set Dark once; every page opens dark; a fresh visitor with a dark phone gets dark everywhere.

title: Small print that cannot be enlarged, and text that ignores the reader's own font-size setting
composition_or_verse: Labels at 9–11 px; meanings at 14–16 px with no control (only Gurmukhi size can be changed); 0 of 401 sampled text elements in each reader scale with the browser's default font size
evidence: reviews/claude-independent/evidence/a02_contrast_targets.json, reviews/claude-independent/evidence/ua_remaining.json (A06_root_font_scaling).
why_it_matters: Elderly readers are a core audience.
proposed_correction: One "Text size" control that scales Gurmukhi, meanings and labels together; sizes in relative units; nothing under 12 px.
acceptance_test: At the largest setting meanings are at least 20 px; with the browser default at 200% all text grows.

title: Finding a place: one long flat list, no search
composition_or_verse: Jaap Sahib: 199 unlabelled English items ("Chhand 1 … Chhand 199"); no search anywhere; the home page link to Japji is a 17 px line at the very bottom
evidence: Screenshot reviews/claude-independent/evidence/screenshots/09_jump_dialog.png.
why_it_matters: A learner looking for a remembered line cannot find it.
proposed_correction: Group by chhand type with Gurmukhi names; add first-letter and text search working offline.
acceptance_test: Any line can be reached by typing its first letters; Jaap list grouped under its 22 chhand headings.

title: Saving a line works three different ways and is hidden in two readers
location: nitnem/index.html (#bookmark inside the tools sheet), js/japji-full.js, js/sukhmani-reader.js
composition_or_verse: Sukhmani: tap a line → "Bookmark this line". Nitnem: open the ⌃ sheet → "☆ Save current line". Japji: no save control is visible while reading and tapping a line does nothing
evidence: reviews/claude-independent/evidence/u09_u15.json.
why_it_matters: Saving a line that moved you is the most personal act in the app.
proposed_correction: One way everywhere: tap or long-press a line → Save · Note · Meaning.
acceptance_test: Same gesture saves a line in all nine compositions, found without instructions by a first-time tester.

title: Other use notes
composition_or_verse: Landscape: header and control bar take about 39% of the height in the Nitnem reader (reviews/claude-independent/evidence/screenshots/62_landscape_nitnem-jaap.png). Resume: Japji reopens about three lines early; Sukhmani asks first; Nitnem is exact. The Nitnem reader does not name the source of Savaiye, Chaupai, Anand or Sohila on screen.
evidence: reviews/claude-independent/evidence/ua_remaining.json, u09_u15.json.
why_it_matters: Polish.
proposed_correction: Auto-hide furniture in landscape; exact resume everywhere; name the source on screen.
acceptance_test: Covered by the unified reader tests.
retest: Device-test preparation, 2026-11-26 (a later note, not a re-test). The Japji sentence of this entry — "reopens about three lines early" — is now registered separately as CI-R-11 (medium): it was found to happen on every reload or Back, and to be saved, so the place keeps moving back. The rest of this entry is unchanged.

title: Sukhmani Sahib is one very heavy page
composition_or_verse: 3.16 MB of files (625 kB compressed) before the first line; 24,600 page elements; first Meaning switch in a Nitnem reader fetches a further 2.3 MB (503 kB compressed)
evidence: Measured in this review. On a slow-connection lab profile with uncompressed local serving the first Sukhmani line took 65.7 s; from the compressed size the real figure is estimated at about 13 s (estimate, not measured). reviews/claude-independent/evidence/r06_slow.json.
why_it_matters: Families on older phones or weak mobile data wait, and older phones may struggle with so large a page.
proposed_correction: Load one ashtpadi at a time; split teaching text per ashtpadi; show Gurbani first.
acceptance_test: First line within 3 s on the slow profile from a real compressed host; memory stays flat while scrolling.

title: Screen-reader users cannot hear the meanings
composition_or_verse: All readers — 62 buttons in Sohila, 387 in Japji, 2,028 in Sukhmani
evidence: Each meaning is a button whose spoken name is replaced by a fixed phrase ("Meaning for this line. Tap to explore.", "Study this passage: …"), so the meaning text itself is not announced. Automated scan: reviews/claude-independent/evidence/a01_axe.json. Not confirmed with VoiceOver (none available).
why_it_matters: Blind and low-vision readers — the people a spoken interface serves most — get no meanings at all. Fails WCAG 2.5.3 and 4.1.2.
proposed_correction: Remove the override so the button's own text is its name; add the hint as a separate description.
acceptance_test: Automated scan clean; VoiceOver on a physical iPhone reads the English and Punjabi meaning.
retest: Re-test RT-001, 2026-11-25, candidate PR #40 at 09e829e (unmerged; the public app is unchanged). FIXED IN THE BROWSER; ONE CRITERION REMAINS. All 3,773 meaning buttons (Japji 385, Sukhmani 2,027, Nitnem 1,361) now give assistive technology a name containing the English and the Punjabi meaning; none carries a fixed label. The original scan falls from 62, 387 and 2,028 failing elements to 6, 2 and 1, none of them a meaning. Remaining, from this finding's own acceptance test: VoiceOver on a physical iPhone, which no one has run. Sukhmani's 2,027 line-buttons (CI-A-02) are unchanged. Record: retests/RT-001_PR40_FIRST_REPAIRS.md.

title: Sukhmani: 2,027 lines of Gurbani are each a button and a keyboard stop
composition_or_verse: Sukhmani Sahib
evidence: 4,089 focusable elements in Meaning view; 2,027 uses of a label on an element that may not carry one. reviews/claude-independent/evidence/a01_axe.json.
why_it_matters: A screen-reader user hears "button" 2,027 times; a keyboard user cannot move through the bani.
proposed_correction: Lines are text; offer one "line actions" control per line or a single roving focus.
acceptance_test: Fewer than 60 focus stops per ashtpadi; scan clean.

title: Minor contrast and touch-target shortfalls
location: nitnem/reader.css (collection numbers #9c865c on #faf7ee = 3.28:1); pauri-2-lesson.html (two labels 4.07:1); several text links under 24 px tall ("Back to the library" 15 px; 32 small links in Japji study; home Japji link 17 px)
composition_or_verse: Nitnem collection page, Pauri 2 lesson, Japji study
evidence: reviews/claude-independent/evidence/a02_contrast_targets.json.
why_it_matters: Small, cheap to fix.
proposed_correction: Darken two colours; give links 44 px touch height.
acceptance_test: All text ≥ 4.5:1; all targets ≥ 24 px, primary ones ≥ 44 px.

title: Checks that passed in emulation
composition_or_verse: No sideways scrolling at 320 px on any page or depth; visible focus ring on every stop; all three dialogs keep focus inside, close on Escape and return focus; reduced-motion setting removes transitions; Gurmukhi is tagged as Punjabi; pinch-zoom is not blocked; Gurbani contrast 11–15:1
evidence: reviews/claude-independent/evidence/ua_remaining.json, reviews/claude-independent/evidence/a02_contrast_targets.json.
why_it_matters: Solid base.

title: Not tested by anyone on this review: a real iPhone, Safari, VoiceOver, TalkBack
composition_or_verse: whole app
evidence: This review used headless Chromium with phone emulation only.
why_it_matters: The app is aimed at the iPhone Home Screen. Emulation cannot show Apple's text drawing, storage rules or VoiceOver behaviour.
proposed_correction: A one-hour scripted device session by a person with an iPhone (script supplied in deliverable 6).
acceptance_test: Checklist completed with photos or screen recordings.

title: Two of the three readers will display altered or incomplete Gurbani with no warning
location: js/japji-full.js, js/sukhmani-reader.js (no run-time check); nitnem/reader.js:24–66 (has one); README.md ("Every source record is checked against its stored hash")
composition_or_verse: Japji Sahib and Sukhmani Sahib readers
evidence: With the data file changed in transit: Japji showed "ਹੁਕਮ ਰਜਾਈ ਚਲਣਾ" for "ਹੁਕਮਿ ਰਜਾਈ ਚਲਣਾ"; Sukhmani showed "ਦੁਖੁ ਪਾਵਉ" for "ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਵਉ" and, in another run, 2,026 lines instead of 2,027 — all with no message. The Nitnem reader refused all eight kinds of tampering. reviews/claude-independent/evidence/r04_corrupt_package.json; screenshots reviews/claude-independent/evidence/screenshots/65_…, 66_…, 60_….
why_it_matters: The assignment requires that a corrupted or incomplete scripture package must not silently render as valid. The only protection for these two readers is the offline installer's check, which does not cover the first visit or a browser without it.
proposed_correction: Give all readers the Nitnem reader's check (whole-file hash, per-line hash, expected counts) and refuse to show text that fails.
acceptance_test: The tamper script reports "refused" for every variant in all three readers.
retest: Re-test RT-001, 2026-11-25, candidate PR #40 at 09e829e (unmerged; the public app is unchanged). REPRODUCED AND FIXED, for everything this finding named. The original tamper script now reports "refused" for every variant in all three readers (Nitnem 8 of 8 as before; Japji 3 of 3; Sukhmani 2 of 2). A wider test — 21 kinds of alteration per reader, to the file in transit and to the text in memory — was refused 21 of 21 by both readers; the published version showed altered text in 5 of the 21 and a wrong number of lines in others. A damaged offline copy is refused. Genuine text opens online and offline, in Chromium and in the WebKit engine. Emulation only: no device. Found alongside and registered separately: CI-R-07, CI-R-08. Record: retests/RT-001_PR40_FIRST_REPAIRS.md.

title: Japji reader silently deletes a saved note or bookmark it cannot place
location: js/continuous-core.js:23 (normalise); README.md ("unknown or damaged saved records are preserved")
composition_or_verse: Japji Sahib reader
evidence: A saved record containing a note on a line ID the reader does not know was cleaned and written back on load: the note was gone and no message appeared. Notes are also cut at 12,000 characters. (Records that were unreadable or of the wrong version were kept safely.) reviews/claude-independent/evidence/d_tests_japji_sukhmani.json.
why_it_matters: Private reflections are the one thing the app cannot recreate. Today this needs an unusual record; it becomes ordinary the day any line ID changes.
proposed_correction: Never drop: move unknown items to a "kept aside" list the reader can see and export.
acceptance_test: The same test shows the note preserved and visible; no silent truncation.
retest: Re-test RT-001, 2026-11-25, candidate PR #40 at 09e829e (unmerged; the public app is unchanged). PARTLY FIXED. Fixed: opening a record no longer drops or cuts anything — notes and bookmarks on unknown lines, notes over 12,000 characters and colliding notes are kept whole, shown on the Saved-learning screen, included in the backup, and survive wipe-and-restore (restoring twice changes nothing). Remaining: (1) RT1-01 — kept-aside items are destroyed without a word when an older copy of the reader opens the same record: a rollback to the published version, or a tab left open from before the update. (2) CI-R-09 — the notice is not on screen for a returning reader in 3 of 4 situations. Record: retests/RT-001_PR40_FIRST_REPAIRS.md. ‖ Re-test RT-002, 2026-11-26, candidate PR #40 at 1470477 (unmerged; the public app is unchanged; emulation only, no device). BOTH REMAINING PARTS FIXED. RT1-01: the three made-up kept-aside items survive a rollback and an old tab, with the published reader and with the first candidate as the older copy, and come back through export, an emptied browser and import; the count does not grow when the same backup is imported three times. CI-R-09: see that entry. Record: retests/RT-002_PR40_SECOND_REPAIRS.md.

title: Nitnem reader: a note on a line that no longer exists stops all saving, and notes under an older edition name disappear from view
composition_or_verse: All six Nitnem readers
evidence: Tested with synthetic data: saving pauses with no way to repair it inside the app; a record stored under an edition ID not listed as a previous one is not shown and not mentioned; without the browser's locking feature nothing is saved at all, not even the reading place. reviews/claude-independent/evidence/d_tests_nitnem2.json.
why_it_matters: Correcting scripture (CI-S-06, CI-S-10) changes line and edition IDs. Without a migration path, the corrections would cost readers their notes.
proposed_correction: Build and test migration before any scripture correction ships: map old IDs to new, keep unmatched notes visible, offer export.
acceptance_test: After a test edition change, every synthetic note and bookmark is still reachable.

title: Backups are eight separate files, with no single "back up everything" and no reminder
composition_or_verse: Storage keys glp001.reader.v1, glp001.fullJapji.v1, glp001.continuous.v2, glp001.sukhmani.v1 and six Nitnem keys
evidence: Observed in all readers. On iPhone, Safari may clear a website's saved data after seven days without a visit unless the app is on the Home Screen (platform rule; not testable here). Only the Japji information sheet mentions exporting before moving to the Home Screen.
why_it_matters: A family could lose years of reflections without ever having been told to back up.
proposed_correction: One backup file for the whole library; a gentle reminder after new notes; plain explanation of the Home Screen point.
acceptance_test: One export restores everything on a clean browser; reminder appears after the first note.

title: Maintenance risks
composition_or_verse: Two copies of the same core file already differ (maximum size 48 vs 60). The whole library (7.2 MB, about 1.5 MB compressed) downloads in the background on the first visit, even from the home page, without saying so.
evidence: File comparison and network log in this review.
why_it_matters: Drift causes bugs; silent downloads cost data.
proposed_correction: One shared file; say "Saving the library for offline use (1.5 MB)".
acceptance_test: One copy; visible offline notice.

title: Checks that passed in emulation: offline, updates, failed update, Nitnem saved learning
composition_or_verse: All 56 offline entries match their hashes; every page and all nine compositions open offline after one visit; a new version waits for the reader; a broken update leaves the old version working, offline too; typed-but-unsaved text is saved before an update; Nitnem export → wipe → import returns every note and bookmark; eleven hostile import files refused; two tabs cannot overwrite each other; a full-storage error is reported
evidence: reviews/claude-independent/evidence/r02_r03_update.json, reviews/claude-independent/evidence/d_tests_nitnem.json, reviews/claude-independent/evidence/d_tests_nitnem2.json.
why_it_matters: The engineering here is careful and worth keeping.

title: The project has no licence, and two of its text sources have no formal notice
location: repository root (no LICENSE); vendor/opengranth/LICENSE and NOTICE exist
composition_or_verse: whole project
evidence: File listing at the baseline commit.
why_it_matters: Without a licence nobody else may legally reuse the work, which contradicts a gift "for humanity"; source projects deserve credit on their own terms.
proposed_correction: Owner decision: choose licences for code and for the original teaching text (they can differ); add notices for BaniDB and SriGranth as their terms require.
acceptance_test: LICENSE files present; notices checked against each source's terms.

title: Small security and housekeeping points
location: pauri-2-lesson.html (allows inline styles in its security policy); index.html (a frame rule placed where browsers ignore it — console error); most pages set no referrer policy; manifest.webmanifest and robots.txt carry out-of-date descriptions; 28 draft pull requests (#4–#33) are open
composition_or_verse: whole project
evidence: Observed in this review (console log, file contents, GitHub API).
why_it_matters: Low risk today; tidy before growth.
proposed_correction: Tighten the two policies; refresh descriptions; close or label stale drafts.
acceptance_test: Policy scan clean on all pages; descriptions current.

title: Checks that passed: nothing leaves the device
composition_or_verse: No request to any other website in any tested flow; no cookies, analytics or remote fonts; notes are shown as text, never run as code; outgoing links cannot reach back; no secrets or personal data in the repository
evidence: Network logs from every browser script in this review; repository scan.
why_it_matters: This is the app's strongest promise and it holds.

title: Not yet verified: that the public website serves exactly the reviewed files
composition_or_verse: whole site
evidence: This review's environment could not reach the public site. GitHub's own record says commit a3476ac was deployed successfully; all testing was on that commit served locally.
why_it_matters: A small gap between "tested" and "what families open".
proposed_correction: Anyone with a normal connection can run the supplied hash check against the live site.
acceptance_test: Live files match evidence/baseline-sha256.txt.

title: No qualified human has reviewed any Gurbani text or any meaning
composition_or_verse: whole library
evidence: The app says so itself; this review confirms the files say 0.
why_it_matters: Every digital check in this review, however complete, is a check of copying — not of correctness.
proposed_correction: Recruit two or three qualified reviewers; give them the focused packet in deliverable 2 (the 138 differing Dasam occurrences first).
acceptance_test: Signed review records exist for each composition.

title: The Nitnem reader keeps a permanent header, against the design decision already accepted for this project
location: nitnem/index.html, nitnem/reader.css; docs/CLAUDE_REVIEW_DECISIONS_20261023.md (decision 2: "One quiet dock, no persistent header")
composition_or_verse: All six Nitnem readers
evidence: A 71 px header stays on screen in the Nitnem reader; the Japji and Sukhmani readers have none. In landscape, header plus dock leave about 61% of the height for Gurbani (reviews/claude-independent/evidence/screenshots/62_landscape_nitnem-jaap.png, reviews/claude-independent/evidence/ua_remaining.json). The same ledger asked for a design review before each promotion; no such review of the Nitnem release is recorded in the repository.
why_it_matters: The newest and largest part of the app departs from the reading design the owner approved, and was published without the agreed check.
proposed_correction: Bring the Nitnem reader to the single-dock design (best done by unifying the readers, CI-U-01).
acceptance_test: No fixed header in any reader; the dock is the only persistent control.

title: Five of the six source-comparison files the builder's audit cites are not in the repository, and the "printed source" it relied on is not named
composition_or_verse: Jaap, Savaiye, Chaupai, Anand, Sohila, Rehras
evidence: Cited but absent: jaap-direct-banidb-comparison.json, jaap-historical-variant-analysis.json, savaiye-direct-provider-comparison.json, chaupai-direct-provider-comparison.json, sggs-source-comparison.json. Present: rehras-sggs-ang-mapping.json. The words "printed", "gutka" and "pdf" do not occur in the source manifest, although six corrections are described as supported by "the visually checked printed source".
why_it_matters: Claims such as "808 occurrences agree exactly with direct BaniDB" and "printed-supported" cannot be checked by anyone else. Evidence that is cited should be kept.
proposed_correction: Commit the five files (or regenerate them) and name the printed edition, publisher, year and pages.
acceptance_test: Every file named in an audit exists at the cited path; the printed edition is named.

title: Where the builder's own records and this review agree
composition_or_verse: whole library
